name: Virus on a Network
miniText: The scientific question is whether contact structure and periodic detection change infection persistence. In NetLogo's Virus on a Network model, susceptible nodes can become infected through neighbors, while checks may remove infection and sometimes produce permanent resistance. The selected literature connects this mechanism to network-mediated contagion and control: graph epidemiology supplies a computer-virus transmission framework [1]; degree heterogeneity can change epidemic spreading behavior [2]; classical epidemic compartments clarify recovery and immunity assumptions [3]. The susceptible-infected-resistant rules and scheduled checking differ from many continuous-time epidemic equations; computer-network interpretation is an analogy. The original NetLogo behavior is the baseline for reimplementation. This simulation offers a controlled thought experiment, and agreement with its output does not establish empirical validation.

verification.evidenceSummary: Abstract (1) One of the most striking features in the study of epidemics is the difficulty of finding a causal factor which appears to be adequate to account for the magnitude of the frequent epidemics of disease which visit almost every population. It was with a view to obtaining more insight regarding the effects of the various factors which govern the spread of contagious epidemics that the present investigation was undertaken. Reference may here be made to the work of Ross and Hudson (1915-17) in which the same problem is attacked. The problem is here carried to a further stage, and it is considered from a point of view which is in one sense more general. The problem may be summarised as follows: One (or more) infected person is introduced into a community of individuals, more or less susceptible to the disease in question.
